title: Counterfactual Blindness: Activation Monitors Miss Model-Internal Reasoning About Oversight

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The distinction between what a model does and what it would do if unobserved is central to alignment. If interpretability cannot access counterfactual reasoning about oversight, it misses the most safety-critical internal states.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Crafting prompts about hypothetical vs. actual oversight and measuring activations at intermediate positions is feasible with TransformerLens. Attention head analysis is documented. Main challenge is that small models may not exhibit meaningful counterfactual reasoning.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear experimental design: compare activations on counterfactual-oversight vs. direct prompts. Attention head analysis adds scope but is optional. The core comparison is tight, though the results may be inconclusive on small models.
